title: Church History II: The Reformation to the Present
description: The story of the church from the Reformation to today. Students study Luther, Zwingli, Calvin and the Radical Reformation, the English Reformation, the Catholic Reformation and Trent, confessionalization and the wars of religion, Puritanism and Pietism, the Evangelical Awakenings and Wesley, the modern missionary movement, the challenges of the Enlightenment and liberalism, the rise of Pentecostalism, Vatican II, the ecumenical movement and the global church. Students read Reformation-era primary sources and confessions from the library.

quiz_bank.answer_key: Struggling with God's righteousness as punishing justice, Luther came to understand from Romans 1:17 that the righteousness of God is the gift by which God justifies sinners through faith; this freed him and grounded his teaching of justification by grace through faith alone.

quiz_bank.question: Summarize the course of the English Reformation.
quiz_bank.answer_key: Henry VIII broke with Rome over his annulment (1534) but kept much Catholic doctrine; under Edward VI Protestant reform advanced (Cranmer's Prayer Books); Mary I restored Catholicism and executed Protestants; Elizabeth I established a moderate Protestant settlement (1559; Thirty-Nine Articles).

quiz_bank.question: What did the Puritans contribute to Christianity?
quiz_bank.answer_key: Emphasis on Scripture, preaching, the regulation of worship by Scripture, personal and family piety, Sabbath observance, pastoral theology, covenant theology, the Westminster Standards, and migration to New England.

quiz_bank.question: Summarize Trent's teaching on justification.
quiz_bank.answer_key: Justification begins with prevenient grace; the sinner cooperates, is justified by the infusion of grace in baptism (making one inwardly righteous), grows by good works, may lose grace by mortal sin and recover it through penance; faith alone as trust in God's mercy is condemned.

quiz_bank.question: What reforms did Trent enact beyond doctrine?
quiz_bank.answer_key: Required seminaries for training priests, residence of bishops, preaching, catechisms (the Roman Catechism), reform of clerical discipline and abuses such as selling indulgences, and a standardized liturgy (the Tridentine Mass).

quiz_bank.question: Describe the main features of Protestant liberalism.
quiz_bank.answer_key: Starting from religious experience or ethics rather than revealed doctrine, embracing historical criticism, questioning miracles and traditional doctrines, emphasizing Jesus as moral teacher and the kingdom as ethical society, and optimism about human progress.

quiz_bank.question: How did Hodge respond to rationalism?
quiz_bank.answer_key: He argued reason must judge the credibility of revelation and may not contradict it, but reason cannot be the source or ultimate measure of theology; Scripture's teachings, attested by the Spirit, are authoritative even when above reason.

quiz_bank.question: Summarize the major developments of the twentieth-century church.
quiz_bank.answer_key: Explosive growth in the global South and of Pentecostalism; the ecumenical movement; Vatican II's renewal of Catholicism; evangelical global mission (Lausanne); martyrdom under totalitarian regimes; secularization and decline in the West.
